item.title: [New] Cross-tenant calendar sharing on Cross-Tenant Access Policy slips to 30 October; EWS-based Free/Busy, MailTips and calendar sharing keep breaking as EWS is disabled
item.description:
Partners lose sight of free/busy and shared calendars as EWS reaches the tenant; the usual workaround — re-enabling EWS — keeps a legacy, high-privilege API surface open for another five months.

Exchange Online · Run Get-OrganizationRelationship and Get-SharingPolicy as the post shows; migrate Free/Busy and MailTips now and Calendar Sharing after 30 October, and if you set EWSEnabled to True, record it as a time-boxed exception ending 1 April 2027.

item.title: [New] Exchange Online: the Change Optics report, which shows the traffic an upcoming service change would affect, is generally available
item.description:
Mail-flow enforcement changes (connector, authentication and sender rules) break traffic you did not know about; a report of affected traffic before enforcement is the evidence to prepare for that.

Exchange Online · Have the messaging team open the report and check which of your connectors or senders it lists before the next Exchange enforcement date.

item.title: [New] Exchange Online: users can send from any of their mailbox's aliases once an admin turns it on (generally available)
item.description:
Once enabled, the From address of outbound mail can be any alias rather than the primary address, so DLP rules, transport rules and hunting queries that match on the primary SMTP address miss mail sent from an alias.

Exchange Online · Before enabling it, review transport and DLP rules and advanced hunting queries on EmailEvents that key on SenderFromAddress for the primary address only, and decide whether aliases should be allowed tenant-wide.

item.title: [New] Exchange Server can become unstable after the October 2026 Windows updates; OWA may fail with MapiExceptionMdbOffline
item.description:
An Exchange outage straight after patching can look like an attack on OWA or a database failure. Knowing it is a reported post-update issue saves an incident escalation, and uninstalling a security update to cure it reopens what that update closed.

Windows Server · If you run Exchange Server on-premises and installed the October 2026 Windows updates, read the post before removing any update and watch OWA and mailbox database availability (inferred: Microsoft's remedy was not in the part of the post read here).

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Exchange Online stops returning selected properties from Get-Mailbox -Migration on 15 November and blocks setting them through New-Mailbox -Migration on 15 December
item.description:
Mailbox-migration and onboarding scripts that read these properties will get empty values without an error, so a provisioning or audit job can silently produce wrong output.

Exchange Online · Search automation, runbooks and third-party migration tools for Get-Mailbox -Migration and New-Mailbox -Migration before 15 November, compare the properties they read with Microsoft's list, and test the scripts against a tenant where the change has landed.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Microsoft cancels the EWS block for Kiosk, F1 and F3 mailboxes that was due on 1 October 2026
item.description:
Frontline mailboxes keep EWS access, so an EWS client or a token stolen from a Kiosk or F3 user still reaches the mailbox. A licence change made to prepare for the block is no longer needed; the EWSAllowedAppIDs allow list is now the control that limits EWS.

Exchange Online · Do not rely on licensing to keep EWS away from frontline mailboxes. Restrict EWS with EWSAllowedAppIDs and EWSEnabled per mailbox where frontline users do not need it, and keep EWS sign-ins from F-licensed users in your hunting queries.
